summary: Log lookout on Leon Peak, Grand Mesa NF, Mesa County, CO; staffed 1911-1915, then abandoned to lightning; log frame stands with cab gone; reached on foot.

facts.design: Log construction with corrugated sheet metal; built as a 12-foot-square house with a cupola
facts.status_note: Log frame still stands; FFLA marks it standing with the cab no longer in place

access.note: Reached on foot from a trailhead near Trickle Park Reservoir; trip reports describe no closure; no Forest Service statement on access was found

visit.trail_note: About 5 miles round trip from near Trickle Park Reservoir, leaving the trail for boulders; a 2014 trip report says the frame may not bear a climber's weight

events.note: Ranger Clay Wintersteen was to have charge of the station that season
Newspapers of August 1911 describe the station as nearing completion; NHLR gives 1912
Carl Pfeiffer sent up to take charge in August 1912 (paper dated August 23, 1912)
Ben Suchre was at the station in September 1913; a paper reported numerous smokes and no fires in late September 1913
Forest Guard Bloss went to the station for the fire-danger season
Guards stationed only through the summer of 1915 (trip report)
Constant lightning strikes forced abandonment (trip report); NHLR says abandoned after a few years
Registered September 11, 2011 as US 919, CO 18; nominated by Kent Argow

corrections.current: The tower still stands, but its cab is gone (FFLA).
corrections.proposed: The log frame still stands; FFLA marks it standing with the cab no longer in place.
corrections.why: NHLR describes a log frame house, not a tower on legs, and FFLA's asterisk legend ties the note to a cab that is no longer in place.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1912 as the build year. Newspapers from August 1911 describe the station as nearing completion, and a 2014 trip report says 1911 or 1912.
NHLR names the Grand Mesa National Forest. The 1911 to 1919 sources on the West Lookouts page use Battlement National Forest.
NHLR says abandoned after a few years. A trip report dates the last guard season to summer 1915 and attributes the end to lightning.

notes_for_editor: Core history rests on NHLR and the West Lookouts newspaper quotes. The 1915 end of staffing and the lightning abandonment come from one 2014 hiker blog, so treat them as medium. Access is inferred from hiker accounts; no Forest Service statement was found. The 1919 guide quoted on the West Lookouts page describes old road access that is not used in the story. No rental listing for Leon Peak found; the Next Summit article's rental lookout is a different site.
